entries.summary: The utility strip renders on the subtle surface, not the export's inverted band — the largest single block of diff in every pair.
entries.rationale: Owner reprice 2026-08-10 (screenshot comparison): appearance converges — the strip is now inverted like the reference, with the .foot ring pattern carrying the canonical focus ring on the inverted surface (--focus-ring-inverted on every control). The original blocker (no token to restore the ring) had already been solved for the footer; the cure generalises. The kit inverted-ring token contract stays routed with the DS trunk slice.
entries.author: design-lane-implementer

entries.summary: Tone-band block rhythm differs (fluid 40-64 vs the export's flush band + page padding), offsetting everything below the hero in every capture.
entries.rationale: Owner reprice 2026-08-10 (screenshot comparison: 'content size and margins in the green header'): the hero converges on the reference's measured rhythm — band flush, inner padding-block 40px, content inset from the container alone (was: band-pad fluid 40-64 on all four sides, +64px inline inset). Scope: the hero; the remaining bands keep the trunk rhythm pending the next fidelity pass.
entries.author: design-lane-implementer

entries.summary: The facets panel, masthead search and newsletter CTA carry no <form> elements (the export neutered its forms with inline onsubmit handlers).
entries.rationale: Inside the picker's frame a stray Enter-submit would re-navigate the frame and break the in-place re-skin's no-reload invariant; fieldsets and labels carry the semantics without a form, and the demo controls are presentational until wired. Zero pixel cost.
entries.author: design-lane-implementer

entries.summary: The keyword definitions' dash separator is CSS-generated, not a text node inside the dl.
entries.rationale: Export source defect, not reproduced: the bare text node inside the dl is an axe definition-list violation (serious), caught by the specimen matrix's first run. The separator is presentation, so it lives in CSS; visually identical. Upstream home: the export's specimen.html carries the defect for any future consumer — flagged for the next export refresh.
entries.author: design-lane-implementer

entries.summary: Footer blurb reads 'renders identical markup under every brand' where the export claims 'this specimen file is byte-identical'.
entries.rationale: The export's sentence is true of a static file and false of a server-rendered route; carrying it verbatim would put an untruth on the page. Restated to the claim that is true here (identical markup, brand as data).
entries.author: design-lane-implementer

entries.summary: The picker chrome differs from the export's switchboard chrome throughout: native select vs segmented control, responsive 16/10 stage vs scale()-fitted 1280 frame, no contract-stage control.
entries.rationale: Owner ruling 2026-08-10: match the appearance and functionality of the PAGE, not necessarily the chrome for selecting theme and identity — the demo chrome is ours to design from the estate's own patterns. Reference-only pair; judged side by side, never pixel-diffed.
